text:
maria: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection tweak rolled last night we're seeing a consistent +15-30% tail on small gen requests (95th/99th up). pprof points at host-side allocations in proto parsing and streaming coalescing.
aj: Can you paste the pprof top and the stack for the big allocs?
maria: quick dump (alloc_space):

pprof top (alloc_space):
  45.2MB  45.2MB  github.com/golang/protobuf/proto.Unmarshal
  18.8MB  18.8MB  bytes.(*Buffer).Grow
  12.1MB  12.1MB  github.com/ourorg/ingress/streaming.(*Chunker).append
   9.7MB   9.7MB  github.com/ourorg/kvcache/shard.CopyAndLock

stack sample for proto.Unmarshal alloc:```
runtime.allocm
runtime.malg
github.com/golang/protobuf/proto.Unmarshal
github.com/ourorg/ingress/parse.ParseRequest
github.com/ourorg/ingress/handler.Handle
```

maria: Also seeing a lot more small allocations bubbling from tokenization path after we switched the host preproc to sentencepiece wrapper (it creates new byte slices per token op).
kevin: hmm — two likely hotspots: 1) proto.Unmarshal allocations when using the std proto path vs gogoproto; 2) the streaming framing code creates temp buffers on each chunk. The kernel-selection change altered typical sequence lengths and that reduced batching, so per-request host overhead is proportionally larger now.
aj: quick repro plan: run microbench with small seq_len distribution, pprof both cpu and alloc, and toggle kernel selection back to baseline. Use these commands:
```
go test ./ingress -bench BenchmarkServe -run none -benchmem -benchmem -cpu 4
go tool pprof -alloc_space http://localhost:9090/debug/pprof/heap
```

kevin: immediate mitigations: reuse proto message instances, preallocate byte buffers in Chunker, use sync.Pool for tokenization buffers, and avoid extra copies in KV cache copy path (CopyAndLock is doing a deep copy on fallback). Also consider replacing google/protobuf.Unmarshal calls with streaming decode that reuses slices.
jen: can we make a small patch that replaces Chunker.append to write into a preallocated buffer and add a pool for tokenization? low-risk canary to dedicated next.
perf-bot: alert: host_latency_95 increased 22% after 2026-02-18T03:12:00Z deployment (rule: host-latency-regression).
ops-bot: rollback option available at https://deploys.redwood.ai/roll/2148700 — tagging eng-runtime.
kevin: I'll prototype a sync.Pool for token byte slices and change Chunker to use a Grow-once buffer. Sketch:```
var tokenBufPool = sync.Pool{New: func() interface{} { return make([]byte, 0, 4096) }}
// in tokenization path:
b := tokenBufPool.Get().([]byte)
// use b via append
// after use: tokenBufPool.Put(b[:0])
```

aj: also instrument KV cache fallback path. If routing copies the shard map per-request we should switch to ref-counted slices or copy-on-write only on mutation.
maria: I ran a quick A/B on dev: adding token pool + chunker prealloc drops alloc_space by ~28% and 95th latency back to baseline for 1k B payloads. KV copy still needs work.
jen: cool — schedule a canary to dedicated for tomorrow and add a perf test in CI that simulates the observed small-request distribution.
kevin: I'll open the PR for pool+chunker change and a follow-up issue for the KV behavior. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/pull/512
ops-bot: canary created: https://canaries.redwood.ai/2148765 (status: pending)
maria: created JIRA perf ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-1689 — assigned to @kevin, will update with pprof traces and the dev A/B numbers.
aj: nice work team. small follow-ups: add zero-copy proto path evaluation and a synthetic test that exercises fallback routing to catch regression early. :thumbsup:
kevin: noted. I'll add a kvcache microbenchmark and wire it into the perf CI job.
